payload.text: The district runs forty-one buses covering six thousand three hundred students across twenty-two schools. Drivers already carry district-issued Android tablets with a data plan, so we are not buying hardware, and we are not touching the buses' engine systems in any way. What I want is for guardians to see where their child's bus is and to get a heads-up before it reaches their stop. Guardians use their own phones. Attendance is not part of this. The schools have their own system for that and we are not replacing it. Rollout is one route at a time, starting with the two high-school routes in September. And if a bus is running more than about ten minutes behind, the school office should know as well.
One correction on what I said. Guardians should only ever see the bus assigned to their own child, never the whole fleet. The superintendent was firm about that and it is settled.
